clue.text: Ground Force applied to get coveted position

indicators.note: ground is the past tense of grind, so the words that follow are crushed and reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardening television show uses some muscle to win a much-wanted spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground Force' reads as the name of a British TV gardening makeover show, but 'Ground' is the anagram signal and FORCE APPLIED is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for the most honoured or prominent spot, the one everyone would like to occupy.

clue.text: Submitted, being sent across island

indicators.note: says the mailing word stretches across, around, the island letter

parts.note: letters sent by mail are posted

explanation.surface: Someone files a submission while being shipped over to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward an idea for consideration, synonym of proposed or offered.

clue.text: Presses son to support club

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece that supports another sits below it

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A boy is pressed into backing a club.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoothing clothes with a hot appliance is pressing them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Oriental that's abandoned as partner for ever

indicators.note: says the next small word is left out of the eastern word

parts.note: something Oriental is Eastern
an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: An Asian person deserted by a spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as partner' reads like a link phrase, but the little word 'as' is what gets abandoned from the eastern word.
explanation.definitionFit: Without end, an adverb meaning always or perpetually.

clue.text: Celebrity footballers appearing on covers of magazine

indicators.note: in a down clue appearing on means sitting above the next piece

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, the body governing English football

indicators.note: the covers are the outside, so the first and last letters are taken

explanation.surface: Famous football players are pictured on the front of a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Being renowned and widely known, the state of a star, is a synonym for celebrity.

clue.text: Outsider pants, feeling effects of exertion

parts.note: to pant for something is to long for it
after hard effort one feels hot

explanation.surface: An unfancied runner is panting and sweaty after the effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' suggests trousers or panting; it is the verb to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor with little chance of winning, in betting terms an underdog.

clue.text: Deliver brief US state victory over East

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the piece before sits above the next

parts.note: Cal is the short form of California

explanation.surface: A short bulletin reports an American state's victory in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliver' here is giving birth, as a cow does.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving birth to a young cow, a farming sense of delivering offspring.

clue.text: Persistent objections must be raised and initiated

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, so the word is turned around

parts.note: ifs and buts are objections
begun or brought into being, so born

explanation.surface: Persistent complaints need to be voiced and started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' sounds like objections being voiced; it reverses BUTS to STUB.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinately refusing to give way, so someone dogged and persistent.

clue.text: English encounters rising regard

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word reads upwards, so reversed

parts.note: to encounter someone is to meet them

explanation.surface: An Englishman meets a growing respect.
explanation.definitionFit: High respect or admiration, so a noun synonym of regard.

clue.text: Wheelwright's representative?

parts.note: a wheelwright fits spokes to wheels, so he is jokingly a man of spokes, while the familiar word means someone speaking for others

explanation.surface: Who speaks for the craftsman who builds wheels?
explanation.walkthrough: The everyday word for an official mouthpiece is split as SPOKES + MAN, a fitting title for a wheel maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A person chosen to speak on behalf of a group is its representative; the split reading adds the wheel-maker pun.

clue.text: Items for auction will include universal plant

indicators.note: says the auction word wraps around the next piece

parts.note: articles put up at an auction are lots
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: An auction catalogue will include a plant among its items.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film certificate for 'universal', suitable for all audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: The water lily of Asia and Egypt, a flowering aquatic species, is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Part of agreement is a necessary medical infusion

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A contract clause insists some medicine be given by drip.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal tea brewed for its supposed health benefits, so a medicinal infusion of leaves or flowers.

clue.text: Look like dropping soldiers for a small rally

indicators.note: says a piece is let fall out of the phrase before it

parts.note: to look like something is to resemble it
RE is the Royal Engineers, a common crossword abbreviation for soldiers

explanation.surface: Paratroops falling from the sky resemble a small gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping soldiers' suggests a parachute drop, but it means removing RE from RESEMBLE, leaving SEMBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally is to gather or come together, a synonym for collecting as a group.

clue.text: Day's beginning sooner than expected, at great cost

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the opening of the next word is used

parts.note: arriving ahead of time is being early

explanation.surface: Starting the day ahead of schedule turns out to be expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb is an idiom for paying a heavy price, as in paid dearly for the mistake.

clue.text: Turned up, being inclined to follow a team's leader

indicators.note: says the inclined word comes after the other pieces
a leader comes first, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: tended means was inclined to do something

explanation.surface: A player showed up, as he tends to follow the team captain.
explanation.definitionFit: To be present at an event, synonym of turned up or was there.

clue.text: Court women in bedroom finding problem with furniture

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: places the women letter inside the bedroom word

parts.note: a dormitory, or dorm, is a shared bedroom

explanation.surface: Wooing ladies in the bedroom leads to trouble with the furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Beetle larvae that bore into timber are a common pest that damages wooden chairs and tables.

clue.text: City area that's part of court estates

parts.note: the dock is the part of a courtroom where the accused stands
estates are landed properties, lands

explanation.surface: A district lies inside the grounds of a royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: London Docklands is a redeveloped riverside business district in east London.
explanation.definitionFit: An urban district built on former docks, an example of a city zone.

clue.text: Fast food ban here? Never!

parts.note: read playfully, the name sounds like a place that bars quick meals, while it is really where quick meals are sold

explanation.surface: An outraged protest at a proposed prohibition on fast food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' can mean ban, so the name looks like a ban on snacks, which such a place would never have.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafe counter serving light quick meals, so a place where fast food is eaten.

clue.text: Youth is naked and prone to be distant

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters of the word are removed

parts.note: lying flat face down is being prone

explanation.surface: A young person lies unclothed far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is naked' strips YOUTH of its first and last letters, leaving OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote and far from the centre, as with an outlying farm or island, so distant.

clue.text: Soldiers on charge initially concealed bloomer

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: says only the first letter of the next word is used

parts.note: concealed means hid

explanation.surface: Troops charging first kept their blunder hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder; here it is something that blooms, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: An exotic flower, so a crossword-style example of a plant that blooms.

clue.text: I do one chapter that's much admired

parts.note: to do someone is slang for to swindle or con them
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone claims a single chapter of theirs is widely praised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' here is slang for cheat, giving CON.
explanation.definitionFit: Regarded as a famous emblem or classic, as an adjective describing something widely celebrated.

clue.text: My supporter must incorporate grand retinue

parts.note: Cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like My!

indicators.note: says the next piece is taken inside the supporter word

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
G is slang for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone's backer has to take on a large entourage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is an exclamation, matched by COR, British slang for surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A funeral procession, a line of followers in attendance, so a retinue.

clue.text: Struggle, seeing Tory beaten soundly by female

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, the Tory party

indicators.note: says the word is taken by how it sounds, not how it is spelt

parts.note: to be beaten is to be licked

explanation.surface: A Conservative suffers a heavy defeat at the hands of a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' seems to intensify the beating, but it signals that LICKED is taken by its sound; 'by' just places the female beside the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A clash or fight between opposing sides, so a synonym for a struggle.

clue.text: Idiot has look around for rope

indicators.note: says the look word goes round the idiot word

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
an ass is an idiot

explanation.surface: A fool glances about for a length of cord.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy's noosed line for catching cattle, a type of rope.

clue.text: There's nothing in the outskirts of Pinner for this flier

indicators.note: places the zero word inside the outer letters
the outskirts are the edges, so only the first and last letters are used

parts.note: love means a score of nothing in tennis

explanation.surface: No birds are found on the edge of Pinner, a suburb in north-west London.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinner is a London suburb; its outskirts are P and R, around LOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wading bird of fields and shores, so an example of a creature that flies.

clue.text: Behold — there's black gold in Virginia!

indicators.note: says the oil word sits inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia
black gold is a nickname for crude oil

explanation.surface: An exclamation as crude is struck in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: A French interjection meaning there it is, used like look or see.

clue.text: Carve a design in sailing vessel when king's disembarked

indicators.note: says the king letter has got off the boat, so it is removed

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A sailor engraves a pattern on the boat once the king has gone ashore.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave lines into a surface with acid or a tool, so to cut a pattern.

clue.text: Things put back in cosmetics?

indicators.note: says the hidden letters are read backwards
says the letters lie inside the next word

explanation.surface: Are the objects returned among the make-up?
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'cosmetics' run SMETI, which 'put back' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: Articles or objects in a list are things, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Free beer on site, but no seconds, is an anathema

indicators.note: free here means loose and rearranged, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Free beer on offer, but no second helpings: what a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but no seconds' says the letters of BEER ON SITE, less one S, are what 'Free' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase for a pet hate, the person or thing one most detests, like an object of loathing.

clue.text: Quarter European, say newspapers

parts.note: a quarter is one fourth
to say something is to state it

explanation.surface: A quarter of Europeans report what the newspapers say.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional nickname for the press, the journalistic estate beside clergy, nobles and commons.
